advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the caused_by write in `_apply_caused_by` against an existing active caused_by link (mirror `add_dependency`'s `_is_active_link` idempotency) so reopen/re-close does not append duplicate edges.
evidence: src/rebar/graph/_links.py:124: "Write a single LINK event to source_id's directory (no cycle check, no idempotency)."
add_dependency guards the write: src/rebar/graph/_links.py:266 `if _is_active_link(source_id, target_id, relation, tracker_dir): ... return` then :272 `_write_link_event(...)`
transition_close.py:538-539 `if target_status == "closed": _apply_caused_by(...)` runs on every close, including a re-close after reopen
_apply_caused_by writes unconditionally at transition_close.py:389 with no active-link check
advisory.finding: `_apply_caused_by` writes the caused_by edge via `_write_link_event` directly, which (per its own docstring) performs 'no cycle check, no idempotency' — unlike `add_dependency`, which guards with `_is_active_link` before writing. Since `_apply_caused_by` runs on every close (`if target_status == "closed"`), a reopen→re-close cycle (or any repeated close) appends a duplicate `caused_by` LINK event; an explicit `--caused-by` with a different id on re-close adds a SECOND edge rather than replacing the first.
scenarios: Bug closed with --caused-by=X, reopened, re-closed → two identical caused_by edges to X
Bug auto-derives culprit X, reopened, re-closed → duplicate caused_by edge
Re-close with a corrected --caused-by=Y leaves both X and Y as caused_by targets
advisory.suggested_fix: Before calling `_write_link_event`, check `_is_active_link(ticket_id, culprit, "caused_by", tracker)` (or skip if any caused_by edge already exists) and return early on a hit.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm `_find_fixing_commit` selects the actual fixing commit (e.g. the one whose close/verify commit references the bug) rather than any recent bug-tagged work commit.
evidence: blame.py:52-64 `_find_fixing_commit` returns the FIRST record from `git log --format=...` (most recent) whose message `_resolves_to(bug_id)`
blame.py:107 `prefix_ref = f"{fixing}~1"` — blames the tree just before whichever commit was selected
No disambiguation between a fix commit and mid-work commits both carrying `rebar-ticket: <bug>`
advisory.finding: `_find_fixing_commit` returns the most-recent `git log` commit whose message resolves to the bug id, but bug implementation work-commits are commonly tagged with the SAME `rebar-ticket: <bug>` trailer as the fix. If a work commit is more recent than the actual fix, blame runs over the wrong `<commit>~1` tree, skewing or invalidating the culprit derivation.
scenarios: A bug's own fix and its earlier WIP commits all carry `rebar-ticket: <bug>`; the most recent WIP (not the fix) is chosen, so `~1` blames a partially-fixed tree

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that closing a NON-bug ticket with --caused-by (and via the library facade) draws no caused_by link.
evidence: Docstring: 'Only bugs carry the blame-hunt semantics.' (transition_close.py:360-362)
ABSENCE: no test in either new file closes a task/story/epic with --caused-by and asserts _caused_by_targets == []
transition_close.py:390-395 swallows all exceptions and logs a warning; comment 'a failure must NEVER block the close'
blame.py:36-40, 55-56 return None on git/OS errors
ABSENCE: no test injects a failure (unresolvable culprit, raising _write_link_event, or git failure) and asserts the close still returns 0 and the bug is closed
advisory.finding: No test covers the non-bug exclusion contract: closing a non-bug ticket with --caused-by (or the library caused_by=) must draw NO caused_by link. The type-gate at transition_close.py:372-373 is unexercised, so dropping it would go undetected.
merged_from: The central best-effort safety contract — a resolve/write failure NEVER blocks or fails the close — is untested. No test forces derive_caused_by/_write_link_event to fail and asserts the close still succeeds (returncode 0 / status closed with no link).
scenarios: A regression removing the ticket_type gate would draw caused_by links on non-bug closes with no failing test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test creating a 'task' (or 'story') ticket, close it with --caused-by=<id>, and assert _caused_by_targets(tid) == [].

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where a blame single-culprit fixture exists AND an explicit --caused-by=<different-id> is passed, asserting the link targets the explicit id (not the blame culprit).
evidence: Help/docstring: '--caused-by ... (overrides git-blame auto-derivation)' (transition.py help text), 'An explicit ``caused_by`` id wins' (transition_close.py:362)
Override branch transition_close.py:375-379 chooses explicit before blame
test_explicit_caused_by_on_bug_close sets file_impact/commits absent — no competing blame culprit exists to override
test_library_facade_threads_caused_by likewise has no blame fixture
advisory.finding: The 'explicit --caused-by overrides git-blame auto-derivation' contract is not regression-tested: every explicit-value test runs with no blame culprit present, so a regression that ignored the explicit value and used blame instead would still pass.
scenarios: Blame would resolve culprit B while the user passes explicit culprit A; if precedence broke, the link would point at B and no test catches it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reuse the single-culprit fixture from test_blame_autoderives_single_culprit, create a second distinct override ticket, close with --caused-by=<override>, and assert the override (not the blame culprit) is the caused_by target.
